content.content:
1	# andesim-demo
2	
3	Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
4	every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
5	(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).
6	
7	## Prerequisites
8	
9	- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
10	  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
11	- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).
12	
13	## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`
14	
15	Fill in these settings if your paths differ:
16	
17	```Makefile
18	ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
19	TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
20	ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
21	```
22	
23	## Step 2: Build
24	
25	```bash
26	make
27	```
28	
29	Each demo links against the andesim runtime
30	(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
31	runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.
32	
33	## Step 3: Run
34	
35	Run every mode of one demo:
36	
37	```bash
38	make run-hello
39	make run-lm
40	make run-lm_slave
41	make run-lm_dma
42	make run-hvm_slave
43	make run-hvm_dma
44	make run-rvv
45	make run-syscall
46	make run-coremark
47	make run-dhrystone
48	```
49	
50	Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*`,
51	`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*`, `rvv-*`, `syscall-*`, `coremark-*` and
52	`dhrystone-*` targets work the same way):
53	
54	| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
55	|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
56	| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
57	| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
58	| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
59	| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |
60	
61	`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
62	QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
63	small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
64	outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
65	checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
66	On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
67	the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.
68	
69	`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
70	SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
71	DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
72	slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
73	(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
74	memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
75	engines and the content crossed the handoff.
76	
77	`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
78	controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
79	aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
80	ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
81	That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
82	models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
83	bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.
84	
85	The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
86	vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
87	enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
88	its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
89	demo:
90	
91	- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
92	  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
93	  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
94	  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
95	  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
96	- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
97	  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
98	  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.
99	
100	On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
101	each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
102	256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.
103	
104	`demo/rvv` tests the vector unit: the ROI runs an RVV-intrinsic kernel
105	(`<riscv_vector.h>`, strip-mined by `vsetvl` so any VLEN works); the
106	workload is an 8x8x8 int32 GEMM. The QEMU phase stages A/B and a scalar
107	reference; the vsim ROI computes C = A x B on the vector unit and
108	compares. `RVV_OK` means the intrinsic kernel ran right after the
109	handoff, with no V setup code inside the ROI. It is built with
110	`-march=rv64gcv` (the intrinsics need V in the arch string). The kernel
111	is integer on purpose: this engine's VPU is integer-only, so a
112	vector-float op (e.g. `vfmacc.vf`) traps on the RTL even though QEMU
113	accepts it.
114	
115	`demo/syscall` exercises the runtime's syscall channels with one
116	binary: stdout (UART), file io and `gettimeofday()` (HTIF, served
117	host-side -- `fopen`/`fread` hit real files in the working directory),
118	and the exit code (SimControl). The QEMU phase writes a
119	time-of-day-seeded payload to a host file and CLOSES it; the vsim ROI
120	runs a `printf`, reopens and reads the file back, and removes it.
121	`SYSCALL_OK` means both legs talked to the same host filesystem. It
122	also shows the two hybrid rules: close files before the handoff (host
123	file descriptors live in the engine process and do not cross -- closed
124	files do), and put must-run code inside the ROI (a hybrid run ends at
125	the exit trigger, so nothing after the ROI executes; the pass signal on
126	hybrid is the printed `SYSCALL_OK`, while fast and cycle also check
127	main's return value through SimControl).
128	
129	`demo/coremark` runs a real benchmark, EEMBC CoreMark, with the EEMBC
130	sources untouched: the ROI markers live in the port layer
131	(`core_portme.c`), inside `start_time()` and `stop_time()` -- the two
132	functions that already delimit the timed run -- so the hybrid window is
133	exactly the region CoreMark times itself with its own `mcycle` reads.
134	That makes the modes cross-check each other: cycle mode's self-reported
135	`Total ticks` and the hybrid `[andesim] N cycles` figure measure the
136	same region and agree within ~0.5% (the hybrid window starts with cold
137	caches and includes the marker/call boundary). The pc-trigger variant
138	gets the same window from the symbols alone
139	(`--pc-start start_time --pc-end stop_time`). On hybrid the run ends at
140	`stop_time()`'s exit marker, so CoreMark's report (CRCs, validation)
141	prints on fast and cycle only; the hybrid output is just the cycle
142	figure. `ITERATIONS=1` by default -- the CRCs still validate, and each
143	extra iteration adds RTL simulation time.
144	
145	`demo/dhrystone` applies the same recipe to Dhrystone 2.2a (the vsim
146	port, which times with `mcycle`/`minstret` instead of UNIX time APIs):
147	the counter reads moved into `start_time()`/`stop_time()`, which carry
148	the ROI markers outside the reads and double as the
149	`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` symbols. The guest's self-reported `CycleCnt`
150	(cycle mode) and the hybrid `[andesim] N cycles` figure measure the
151	same region; on hybrid the run ends at `stop_time()`'s marker, so the
152	`InstCnt/CycleCnt` line prints on fast and cycle only. `RUNS=1000` by
153	default (`make dhrystone-cycle RUNS=100` for a quicker RTL run); note
154	Dhrystone keeps the two-pass compile rule (`dry.c` builds twice, the
155	second pass with `-DPASS2`).
156	
157	Expected output (hybrid):
158	
159	```
160	hello from andesim!
161	[andesim] 3532 cycles
162	```
163	
164	The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
165	close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.
166	
167	## Debugging a failed run
168	
169	Use andesim's logs -- they are designed to locate the problem:
170	
171	```bash
172	make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 1"   # + per-leg detail
173	make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 0 --log-file run.log"
174	```
175	
176	- `--log-level` uses vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info (default)
177	  3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off.
178	- On a hybrid failure andesim keeps a repro bundle (state files, exact
179	  commands, manifest) under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` and prints its path.
180	
181	## Layout
182	
183	```
184	Make.var        shared configuration (paths, toolchain, engine)
185	Makefile        builds and runs every demo below
186	demo/hello/     hello world on all four modes
187	demo/lm/        ILM/DLM content transport across the hybrid handoff
188	demo/lm_slave/  the same SRAMs through the bus slave-port apertures
189	demo/lm_dma/    a DMA master fills the DLM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
190	demo/hvm_slave/ HVM content transport through the bus subordinate port
191	demo/hvm_dma/   a DMA master fills the HVM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
192	demo/rvv/       RVV-intrinsic kernel (8x8x8 GEMM) inside the ROI

# andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
make run-rvv
make run-syscall
make run-coremark
make run-dhrystone
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*`,
`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*`, `rvv-*`, `syscall-*`, `coremark-*` and
`dhrystone-*` targets work the same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
engines and the content crossed the handoff.

`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.

The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
demo:

- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.

On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/rvv` tests the vector unit: the ROI runs an RVV-intrinsic kernel
(`<riscv_vector.h>`, strip-mined by `vsetvl` so any VLEN works); the
workload is an 8x8x8 int32 GEMM. The QEMU phase stages A/B and a scalar
reference; the vsim ROI computes C = A x B on the vector unit and
compares. `RVV_OK` means the intrinsic kernel ran right after the
handoff, with no V setup code inside the ROI. It is built with
`-march=rv64gcv` (the intrinsics need V in the arch string). The kernel
is integer on purpose: this engine's VPU is integer-only, so a
vector-float op (e.g. `vfmacc.vf`) traps on the RTL even though QEMU
accepts it.

`demo/syscall` exercises the runtime's syscall channels with one
binary: stdout (UART), file io and `gettimeofday()` (HTIF, served
host-side -- `fopen`/`fread` hit real files in the working directory),
and the exit code (SimControl). The QEMU phase writes a
time-of-day-seeded payload to a host file and CLOSES it; the vsim ROI
runs a `printf`, reopens and reads the file back, and removes it.
`SYSCALL_OK` means both legs talked to the same host filesystem. It
also shows the two hybrid rules: close files before the handoff (host
file descriptors live in the engine process and do not cross -- closed
files do), and put must-run code inside the ROI (a hybrid run ends at
the exit trigger, so nothing after the ROI executes; the pass signal on
hybrid is the printed `SYSCALL_OK`, while fast and cycle also check
main's return value through SimControl).

`demo/coremark` runs a real benchmark, EEMBC CoreMark, with the EEMBC
sources untouched: the ROI markers live in the port layer
(`core_portme.c`), inside `start_time()` and `stop_time()` -- the two
functions that already delimit the timed run -- so the hybrid window is
exactly the region CoreMark times itself with its own `mcycle` reads.
That makes the modes cross-check each other: cycle mode's self-reported
`Total ticks` and the hybrid `[andesim] N cycles` figure measure the
same region and agree within ~0.5% (the hybrid window starts with cold
caches and includes the marker/call boundary). The pc-trigger variant
gets the same window from the symbols alone
(`--pc-start start_time --pc-end stop_time`). On hybrid the run ends at
`stop_time()`'s exit marker, so CoreMark's report (CRCs, validation)
prints on fast and cycle only; the hybrid output is just the cycle
figure. `ITERATIONS=1` by default -- the CRCs still validate, and each
extra iteration adds RTL simulation time.

`demo/dhrystone` applies the same recipe to Dhrystone 2.2a (the vsim
port, which times with `mcycle`/`minstret` instead of UNIX time APIs):
the counter reads moved into `start_time()`/`stop_time()`, which carry
the ROI markers outside the reads and double as the
`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` symbols. The guest's self-reported `CycleCnt`
(cycle mode) and the hybrid `[andesim] N cycles` figure measure the
same region; on hybrid the run ends at `stop_time()`'s marker, so the
`InstCnt/CycleCnt` line prints on fast and cycle only. `RUNS=1000` by
default (`make dhrystone-cycle RUNS=100` for a quicker RTL run); note
Dhrystone keeps the two-pass compile rule (`dry.c` builds twice, the
second pass with `-DPASS2`).

Expected output (hybrid):

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

## Debugging a failed run

Use andesim's logs -- they are designed to locate the problem:

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 1"   # + per-leg detail
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 0 --log-file run.log"
```

- `--log-level` uses vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info (default)
  3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off.
- On a hybrid failure andesim keeps a repro bundle (state files, exact
  commands, manifest) under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` and prints its path.

## Layout

```
Make.var        shared configuration (paths, toolchain, engine)
Makefile        builds and runs every demo below
demo/hello/     hello world on all four modes
demo/lm/        ILM/DLM content transport across the hybrid handoff
demo/lm_slave/  the same SRAMs through the bus slave-port apertures
demo/lm_dma/    a DMA master fills the DLM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/hvm_slave/ HVM content transport through the bus subordinate port
demo/hvm_dma/   a DMA master fills the HVM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/rvv/       RVV-intrinsic kernel (8x8x8 GEMM) inside the ROI
demo/syscall/   stdio, host file io and exit code on every mode
demo/coremark/  EEMBC CoreMark; the ROI is the benchmark's own timed region
demo/dhrystone/ Dhrystone 2.2a; same recipe, two-pass compile kept
```

1	# andesim User Guide
2	
3	Audience: an engineer who wants to RUN programs on the Andes simulators
4	through `./andesim` and measure cycle counts. This guide covers every
5	user-facing option and feature.
6	
7	It assumes andesim and its engines are already installed and built
8	(QEMU, the vsim engines, the plugin, the runtime, and the test ELFs are
9	prebuilt). If something is missing, run `./andesim doctor` and hand the
10	report to whoever owns your install; building is covered in `README.md`,
11	not here.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## 1. What andesim is
16	
17	andesim runs one RISC-V ELF on one of three models:
18	
19	| Model    | What runs                              | Speed          | You get                    |
20	|----------|----------------------------------------|----------------|-----------------------------|
21	| `fast`   | QEMU only (functional)                 | MHz-class      | program output, fast        |
22	| `cycle`  | one cycle-accurate engine, from reset  | kHz-class      | program output + total cycles |
23	| `hybrid` | QEMU fast-forwards, then the cycle engine measures one region you choose | fast until your region | program output + cycles of JUST your region |
24	
25	`hybrid` is the headline feature: QEMU races through boot and setup, then
26	hands the complete architectural state and memory to the cycle-accurate
27	engine (vsim, built from the real RTL), which runs only your
28	region-of-interest (ROI). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta
29	across that window. You mark the window with a **trigger**: source-level
30	markers or a pair of PCs (section 5.3).
31	
32	One run models ONE core. The cycle engine defines the hardware (ISA,
33	VLEN, caches); in hybrid mode the QEMU leg automatically inherits that
34	engine's ISA and VLEN so both legs execute the same architecture.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## 2. Check your installation
39	
40	```sh
41	./andesim doctor          # read-only health report
42	./andesim list models     # the three models
43	./andesim list engines    # every engine you can pass to --engine
44	```
45	
46	`doctor` checks artifacts, toolchain, runtime, engines, and the shared-memory
47	backing tiers, and prints WSL2 advice where relevant. A healthy install ends
48	with `Summary: N PASS, 0 FAIL`.
49	
50	`list engines` shows what `--engine` accepts:
51	
52	```
53	ENGINE                 TYPE  KIND            XLEN  VLEN  DLEN  ELEN
54	qemu64                 qemu  functional      64    -     -     -
55	qemu32                 qemu  functional      32    -     -     -
56	vsim:ax45mpv_premium   vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
57	vsim:ax46mpv_advanced  vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
58	```
59	
60	`qemu64`/`qemu32` are the functional engines (`fast`); the `vsim:<cfg>`
61	entries are the cycle-accurate engines (`cycle`, and the measuring leg of
62	`hybrid`). `-` means the engine does not report that parameter.
63	
64	Run `./andesim run -h` any time for the compact flag list; this guide is
65	the long version.
66	
67	---
68	
69	## 3. First runs
70	
71	The install ships ready-made ELFs under `tests/fixtures/`; the examples
72	below use them. Replace with your own ELF once you have one (section 4).
73	
74	### 3.1 fast -- functional, full speed
75	
76	```sh
77	./andesim run --mode fast tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
78	```
79	
80	```
81	hello from vplat
82	```
83	
84	Output is the program's own output, verbatim (QEMU passthrough). The exit
85	code of your program becomes the process exit code.
86	
87	### 3.2 cycle -- one engine, from reset, total cycles
88	
89	```sh
90	./andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
91	```
92	
93	```
94	hello from vplat
95	[andesim] 4247 cycles
96	```
97	
98	The engine's startup banner and verbose info log are filtered out so the
99	result stands alone; real warnings/errors still pass through, and the
100	program's exit code is propagated. The figure is the whole run from reset
101	-- boot, runtime init, everything.
102	
103	### 3.3 hybrid -- fast-forward, then measure your region
104	
105	`hybrid` needs a trigger that says where the measured window starts and
106	ends. The fixture below already contains ROI markers, so `--trigger
107	marker` works out of the box:
108	
109	```sh
110	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
111	  tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
112	```
113	
114	```
115	hello from QEMU1
116	[andesim] 54 cycles
117	```
118	
119	Reading the output:
120	
121	- `hello from QEMU1` is the program's own output from the fast leg.
122	- `[andesim] 54 cycles` is the answer: your ROI took 54 cycles on
123	  this engine. It is the vsim `mcycle` delta across the window (the same
124	  line shape `cycle` mode prints, but here it covers JUST your ROI).
125	- The run ends after the ROI. Code after your ROI never executes in a
126	  hybrid run -- hybrid is a measuring tool, not a way to finish the program.
127	- Want more detail? `--log-level 1` (section 5.10) adds the driver's
128	  chatter: the resolved engine/VLEN/trigger banner and the shared-memory
129	  line (`[andesim] mmap ...`, section 5.4).
130	
131	The first hybrid run of a given (engine, ELF) pair is a few seconds slower:
132	andesim captures the engine's reset state once and caches it under
133	`~/.cache/andesim/` so later runs can skip restoring registers that still
134	hold reset values (typically ~4x faster on the vsim leg). The cache
135	refreshes itself when the engine or the ELF changes.
136	
137	---
138	
139	## 4. Prepare your own program
140	
141	### 4.1 Compile once, run on every engine
142	
143	Link against the andesim runtime and one ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
144	and across a `hybrid` handoff -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting:
145	
146	```sh
147	riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \
148	  -B <andesim>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
149	```
150	
151	- Use your Andes RISC-V GCC (the one `./andesim doctor` reports).
152	- `-B` points gcc at the runtime artifacts; use the absolute path when
153	  compiling outside the repo.
154	- `-specs=andesim.specs` swaps in the runtime's `crt0.o`, links
155	  `andesim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and pins the library order, so no
156	  semihosting library can leak into the link.
157	- Add `v` to `-march` (e.g. `rv64gcv`) for RVV code.
158	
159	For rv32 targets use the rv32 compiler and the rv32 runtime flavor:
160	
161	```sh
162	riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O2 \
163	  -B <andesim>/build/runtime/rv32 -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
164	```
165	
166	Custom build system (no gcc driver)? Link the pieces directly:
167	
168	```sh
169	... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andesim.ld \
170	  build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
171	  -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
172	```
173	
174	What the runtime gives your program, on every engine:
175	
176	| Channel          | Behavior                                                       |
177	|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
178	| stdio (fd 0-2)   | `printf` etc. go to the simulator console (a modeled UART)     |
179	| exit code        | `exit(n)` (n < 256) terminates the simulation; `n` becomes the simulator process exit code |
180	| file io (fd > 2) | `open`/`read`/`write` pass through to host files, resolved against the engine's working directory |
181	
182	A `printf` inside a measured ROI works -- but it adds the real UART cycles
183	to your figure. Keep measured kernels I/O-free when you want clean numbers.
184	
185	### 4.2 Mark your region (ROI markers)
186	
187	For `--trigger marker`, wrap the region you want to measure:
188	
189	```c
190	#include <andesim/ROI.h>   /* shipped with the runtime; rides the -B flag */
191	
192	andesim_ROI_begin();
193	my_kernel(a, b, c);
194	andesim_ROI_end();
195	```
196	
197	The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (architectural NOPs), so a marker
198	binary also runs unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and on real silicon.
199	Ship one binary; measure when you want.
200	
201	> **Measurement hygiene:** keep the kernel anchored inside the marker span
202	> -- read its inputs and write its outputs through memory inside the span,
203	> or wrap the kernel in a `__attribute__((noinline))` function called
204	> between the markers. The markers pin memory I/O but not register-only
205	> compute, so a kernel that carries live values in registers across the
206	> boundary may be hoisted or sunk out of the measured window by the
207	> compiler.
208	
209	### 4.3 Cannot edit the binary? Use PC boundaries
210	
211	`--trigger pc` needs no markers: you name the window with `--pc-start` and
212	`--pc-end`, each a symbol name or a `0x` address (section 5.3). To find
213	the hot region of an unknown binary first, run the bundled detector:
214	
215	```sh
216	./build/hotloops --min-iters 10 my_kernel.elf
217	```
218	
219	It runs the binary fast and reports the hottest loops (function, source
220	line, PC range) with a ready `measure:` line -- a `--pc-start`/`--pc-end`
221	pair you can paste straight into the hybrid command. See `docs/hotloops.md`
222	for the full flag reference.

226	## 5. The `run` options, one by one
227	
228	Synopsis:
229	
230	```
231	./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [options] <ELF> [-- <engine args>]
232	```
233	
234	`run` is the default command -- you may omit it. `./andesim --mode fast
235	my.elf` and `./andesim my.elf --mode fast` both work; only the explicit
236	commands (`list`, `doctor`) are recognized by name.
237	
238	### 5.1 `--mode fast|cycle|hybrid` (required)
239	
240	Picks the model (section 1). Everything else keys off this choice.
241	
242	### 5.2 `--engine <id>`
243	
244	Picks the engine from `./andesim list engines`.
245	
246	- `fast`: optional. The driver auto-selects `qemu64` or `qemu32` to match
247	  your ELF's width; an explicit `--engine qemu32|qemu64` overrides (with a
248	  warning if it disagrees with the ELF).
249	- `cycle` / `hybrid`: names the cycle-accurate engine. Optional only when
250	  exactly one is installed; with several you must choose:
251	
252	  ```
253	  andesim run --mode cycle: model cycle: multiple cycle-accurate engines;
254	  select one with --engine (have: vsim:ax45mpv_premium, vsim:ax46mpv_advanced)
255	  ```
256	
257	Width rules: `cycle`/`hybrid` reject an ELF whose width does not match the
258	engine, up front:
259	
260	```
261	andesim run --mode cycle: ELF is rv32 but engine 'vsim:ax45mpv_premium' is rv64
262	  -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF
263	```
264	
265	Hybrid additionally requires an rv64 engine (the fast leg is rv64; an rv32
266	engine cannot share architectural state with it and is rejected).
267	
268	VLEN: each vsim engine has a fixed VLEN (see `list engines`); in hybrid
269	mode the QEMU leg inherits the engine's ISA and VLEN automatically, so
270	both legs execute identical architecture. Supported VLEN range in hybrid:
271	128 to 1024 bits. A standalone `fast` run defaults to the vector-capable
272	`andes-ax46mpv` (rv64) / `andes-a46mpv` (rv32) CPU model; to pin an exact
273	VLEN there, append a `-cpu` through the passthrough tail (the last `-cpu`
274	wins):
275	
276	```sh
277	./andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax46mpv,vlen=256
278	```
279	
280	### 5.3 `--trigger marker|pc` (+ `--pc-start`, `--pc-end`) -- hybrid only, required
281	
282	The ROI delimiter for `--mode hybrid`.
283	
284	**`--trigger marker`** (recommended when you can edit the source): the
285	window is the span strictly between `andesim_ROI_begin()` and
286	`andesim_ROI_end()` (section 4.2). The markers themselves are NOPs and
287	cost nothing.
288	
289	**`--trigger pc`**: explicit boundaries, no source edits. Both flags are
290	required; each accepts a symbol name or a `0x` hex address:
291	
292	```sh
293	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
294	  --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x1002cc my.elf
295	```
296	
297	Semantics you should know:
298	
299	- The instruction at `--pc-start` executes INSIDE the measured window (the
300	  fast leg stops just before it; the cycle engine resumes at it -- no
301	  instruction is lost across the handoff). `--pc-end` is where the window
302	  closes.
303	- Symbols are resolved from the ELF's own symbol table by the driver; no
304	  toolchain is needed at run time. A name that is not defined fails with
305	  `symbol '<x>' not defined in <elf>`; a bad literal fails with
306	  `malformed address '<x>'`.
307	- Both triggers are one-shot: the first hit of the start boundary opens the
308	  window, the first hit of the end boundary closes it. For a function called
309	  many times, the window is the FIRST call.
310	- Start and end must resolve to different addresses; an equal pair is an
311	  empty window and is rejected up front:
312	  `--pc-start and --pc-end resolve to the same address 0x... (an empty ROI measures nothing)`.
313	
314	### 5.4 `--mem-size <spec>` -- guest memory
315	
316	`SPEC` accepts `256M`, `1.5G`, `2G`, or raw bytes. Per-model meaning:
317	
318	| Model    | Effect |
319	|----------|--------|
320	| `hybrid` | Your program RAM (default `128M`). Max `2G` minus 4 KiB: the driver reserves one page just above your RAM for the vector-register transport, so exactly `2G` is rejected (use `2047M`) and an ELF whose static image reaches into the reserved page is rejected with `raise --mem-size or shrink the image`. |
321	| `fast`   | Forwarded as a plain QEMU `-m`. No 2G cap; QEMU validates the size itself. |
322	| `cycle`  | Ignored (the engine always models its full DRAM window); the driver says so on stderr. |
323	
324	Where the hybrid shared memory lives: andesim allocates a file both legs
325	map. It picks the first tier with enough free space (request + 256 MiB
326	headroom); run with `--log-level 1` to see which:
327	
328	1. `/dev/shm` -- RAM-backed, fastest.
329	2. `~/.cache/andesim` -- disk-backed fallback (honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`).
330	
331	```
332	[andesim] mmap 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))
333	```
334	
335	Set `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/path` to pin one directory with NO fallback past it
336	(the run fails with a hint if it cannot hold the request). Do not pin a
337	tmpfs mount (`/tmp` on some distros) expecting a disk ceiling -- tmpfs is
338	still RAM.
339	
340	### 5.5 `--print-memmap` -- which addresses may a hybrid workload touch?
341	
342	Prints the guest memory map for exactly the run you are about to do (same
343	`--engine`/`--mem-size`; the ELF is optional and only adds a fit note),
344	then exits without running anything. Hybrid only.
345	
346	```sh
347	./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 128M
348	```
349	
350	```
351	[andesim] hybrid memory map: engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium mem-size=128M
352	REGION           BASE         END          SIZE    TRANSPORT
353	DRAM             0x0          0x7ffffff    128M    shared mmap; content survives the handoff
354	V-scratch        0x8000000    0x8000fff    4K      reserved by the hybrid V transport; not program-usable
355	ILM              0x0          0xffff       64K     sidecar .ilm; DRAM overlay while milmb.IEN=1
356	DLM              0x200000     0x207fff     32K     sidecar .dlm; DRAM overlay while mdlmb.IEN=1
357	HVM              0x90000000   0x9003ffff   256K    sidecar .hvm
358	SimControl/HTIF  0xe0080000   0xe0080fff   4K      device; state does not cross the handoff
359	UART2            0xf0300000   0xf03fffff   1M      device (console); state does not cross the handoff
360	```
361	
362	How to read it:
363	
364	- END is the inclusive last byte.
365	- DRAM tracks `--mem-size`; the V-scratch page above it belongs to andesim.
366	- ILM/DLM/HVM rows appear only when the chosen engine has those memories
367	  and can transport their content; the addresses are the engine's own.
368	- Device state never crosses the handoff (each engine has its own UART and
369	  SimControl instance); only RAM content does.
370	- Anything NOT listed is unsupported in hybrid mode: it exists in one
371	  engine only, so touching it inside the ROI gives engine-specific behavior.
372	
373	### 5.6 `--dry-run` -- preview without running
374	
375	Valid in every mode: prints the exact engine command line(s), fully
376	resolved and shell-quoted, and runs nothing. `fast`/`cycle` print one
377	command; `hybrid` prints both legs. Use it to see precisely what a run
378	will execute, or to lift the command for your own scripting.
379	
380	```sh
381	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --dry-run my.elf
382	# [andesim] dry-run: 2 command(s), not executed
383	# # command 1/2: fast-leg [qemu64]
384	# qemu-system-riscv64 ... -plugin .../libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=...
385	# # command 2/2: accurate-leg [vsim:ax45mpv_premium]
386	# sim_ax45mpv_premium my.elf --resume-from-qemu ... --handoff-out ...
387	```
388	
389	### 5.7 `--verify` -- cross-check a hybrid run against a QEMU oracle
390	
391	A hybrid run normally proves only that a cycle figure came out. `--verify`
392	(hybrid only, default off) re-runs the same ELF on pure QEMU up to the ROI
393	exit and compares the architectural state field by field against what the
394	cycle engine drained:
395	
396	```
397	[andesim] 46 cycles
398	[state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match (counters and passthrough CSRs excluded)
399	[verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle
400	```
401	
402	A mismatch lists each differing field and exits non-zero:
403	
404	```
405	[state-diff] x10: ref=0x3d got=0x0
406	[state-diff] FAIL: 1 mismatch(es) (115 fields compared)
407	```
408	
409	What is compared: the PC, all GPRs, FPRs (when FP state is live), the
410	vector registers and V CSRs (when V is live), the privilege level, and the
411	M-mode CSRs that round-trip through the handoff. Deliberately excluded:
412	`mcycle`/`minstret` (the engines count differently by design), `mip`
413	(hardware-driven pending bits), and a few CSRs whose reset values
414	legitimately differ between engines.
415	
416	Two costs: one extra QEMU run of the whole program (cheap), and a full
417	register read-back over the Debug Module at the ROI exit (not cheap --
418	without `--verify` the exit drain reads only the two counters). Expect a
419	`--verify` run to take noticeably longer; the cycle figure itself is not
420	affected.
421	
422	Related, printed on EVERY hybrid run (not just `--verify`): andesim tracks
423	which config CSRs your program actually wrote during the fast leg and
424	warns if any of them do not exist on the chosen cycle engine:
425	
426	```
427	[andesim] warning: the program wrote CSRs engine vsim:<engine> does not
428	implement: <names> (on this engine's silicon these writes would trap; the
429	hybrid restore skipped them)
430	```
431	
432	That means your program, on that engine's real silicon, would trap before
433	the ROI -- pick an engine that implements those CSRs, or drop the writes.
434	A clean run prints nothing.
435	
436	### 5.8 `--kanata <file>` (+ `--objdump <file>`) -- pipeline trace of the ROI
437	
438	Hybrid only (`--trigger marker|pc`). Writes a Kanata-format pipeline trace
439	covering exactly the measured window -- engine boot and handoff overhead
440	are filtered out. Open the file in
441	[Konata](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata) to see the pipeline.
442	
443	```sh
444	./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
445	  --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
446	  --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata
447	```
448	
449	Add `--objdump <file>` (a text dump you generated once with
450	`riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d my.elf > my.S`) and the trace embeds the
451	disassembly next to each PC. `--objdump` requires `--kanata`.
452	
453	Marker-mode constraint: the ELF must contain exactly one exit marker. With
454	more than one, the run errors out and tells you to use `--trigger pc` with
455	an explicit `--pc-end` instead.

457	### 5.9 `--gdb` (+ `--gdb-port <port>`) -- attach a debugger
458	
459	Pauses the simulation at startup so a debugger can attach. Not available
460	in hybrid mode.
461	
462	**fast** -- opens QEMU's GDB stub (default port 1234) and waits:
463	
464	```sh
465	./andesim run --mode fast --gdb my.elf
466	# other terminal:
467	gdb-multiarch -ex 'target remote :1234' my.elf
468	```
469	
470	**cycle** -- resets and HALTS the hart, opens the engine's JTAG bitbang
471	port (default 9104) in the background, then execs `$ICEMAN` -- your JTAG
472	debug server -- in the foreground. Point GDB at the server's own gdb port
473	(from your server config), not at 9104:
474	
475	```sh
476	export ICEMAN=/path/to/jtag-debug-server
477	./andesim run --mode cycle --gdb --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium my.elf
478	```
479	
480	`$ICEMAN` must speak the OpenOCD `remote_bitbang` protocol. A modern
481	**OpenOCD (0.12+)** works: a one-line wrapper can `exec openocd -f <cfg>`
482	where `<cfg>` sets `adapter driver remote_bitbang`, `remote_bitbang port
483	9104`, a generic `riscv` target, and a `gdb_port`. Note: the OpenOCD 0.10
484	bundled with Andes ICEman has a `remote_bitbang` bug against this DTM --
485	use a current OpenOCD.
486	
487	`--gdb-port` overrides the port (fast: the QEMU stub port; cycle: the
488	JTAG bitbang port).

490	### 5.10 `--log-level <0-6>` (+ `--log-file`) -- how much andesim says
491	
492	The same scale as the vsim engines' own `--log-level`, so you learn one
493	scheme: `0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off`.
494	Default is `2` (info): you see your program's output, the answer line
495	(`[andesim] N cycles`), and any warnings or errors -- nothing else.
496	
497	`--log-level 1` (debug) adds the driver's chatter: the hybrid banner
498	(engine/VLEN/trigger), the decision lines (which engine and why; what
499	your `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` resolved to), the shared-mmap line (section
500	5.4), the window detail (`[andesim] window: trigger=... vsim mcycle=...
501	qemu mcycle=...`), and the closing PASS line. The level also rides into
502	both hybrid legs: the vsim engine gets the same `--log-level`, the QEMU
503	handoff plugin gets `log_level=`, and their stderr streams live to your
504	terminal (at info and above it is silenced), so one flag tunes the whole
505	pipeline.
506	
507	`--log-level 0` (trace) additionally prints, just before each engine
508	spawns, its fully resolved command line -- the hybrid legs (`[andesim]
509	exec fast-leg [qemu64]: ...`) and the standalone fast/cycle runs
510	(`[andesim] exec standalone [qemu64]: ...`) alike. It is the same text
511	`--dry-run` shows, copy-pasteable to re-run one engine by hand, and it
512	is emitted BEFORE the spawn, so even a hung run leaves the command in
513	the log.
514	
515	`--log-file <file>` appends EVERY level's messages -- timestamped and
516	level-tagged, regardless of the console `--log-level` -- to `<file>`.
517	Run once with `--log-file`, attach the file to a bug report, and nothing
518	needs re-running. Your program's own output is never filtered at any
519	level.
520	
521	Related (always on, any level): when a hybrid leg fails, andesim keeps
522	the run's evidence -- the drained state files, LM sidecars, the staged
523	QEMU config, a copy of your ELF, and a `manifest.txt` with the error and
524	every leg's exact command -- under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` (newest 20
525	kept) and prints where:
526	
527	```
528	[andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at /home/u/.cache/andesim/repro/20260711T081500Z-my_prog (see manifest.txt)
529	```
530	
531	### 5.11 `-- <args...>` -- engine passthrough
532	
533	Everything after a bare `--` is forwarded verbatim to the engine.
534	`fast`/`cycle` only: those modes run one engine process, so there is an
535	unambiguous target (see the VLEN example in 5.2). `hybrid` builds both
536	legs' command lines itself and REJECTS `--` args rather than guessing
537	which leg you meant -- use the dedicated flags (`--kanata`, `--objdump`,
538	`--mem-size`, ...) instead.

542	## 6. What a hybrid run does for you automatically
543	
544	You normally do not need this section to use andesim -- it explains the
545	behaviors you will observe.
546	
547	**Two legs, one state.** The fast leg (QEMU) runs to your ROI start, then
548	drains the complete architectural state -- GPRs, FPRs, vector registers,
549	CSRs (including the Andes-specific blocks), privilege level -- into a
550	state file. Program RAM is shared by construction (both legs map the same
551	file), so memory needs no copy. The cycle engine restores the state
552	through its Debug Module, runs your ROI, and drains the counters at the
553	exit trigger. The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta.
554	
555	**Config that matters for timing rides along.** Cache-enable state (L1
556	`mcache_ctl`, and the L2 controller's config window on engines that have
557	an L2) is restored before the ROI, so a program that enabled caches during
558	boot measures WITH caches on -- not at the engine's reset default.
559	
560	**Only what your program wrote is restored.** andesim records which config
561	CSRs the program actually wrote during the fast leg and restores only
562	those; an untouched CSR keeps the engine's own reset value, exactly like
563	that engine's real silicon. If the program wrote a CSR the engine does not
564	implement, you get the warning shown in section 5.7.
565	
566	**Local memories travel too.** On engines with ILM/DLM (tightly-coupled
567	memories) or HVM (high-bandwidth vector memory), their content is drained
568	from the fast leg and loaded into the cycle engine before resume, so a
569	program that stages code or data there before the ROI resumes with it in
570	place. (A program using ILM/DLM must enable them itself via
571	`milmb`/`mdlmb`, as real TCM firmware does; that write is restored
572	automatically.) `--print-memmap` shows whether your engine has these
573	regions.
574	
575	**First-run baseline capture.** Restoring a register over the Debug Module
576	costs hundreds of simulated cycles, and most state still holds reset
577	values. The first hybrid run of a given (engine build, ELF) pair captures
578	the engine's reset state once and caches it under `~/.cache/andesim/`
579	(honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`); later runs skip the no-op restores, typically
580	cutting the vsim leg ~4x. The cache invalidates itself when the engine or
581	ELF changes; delete the directory to force a fresh capture. This never
582	changes results -- a restore is skipped only when the value is already
583	there.
584	
585	**The ROI envelope (limits).** The measured window is assumed bare-metal,
586	single-hart, trap-free, interrupt-free, paging-off, and single-privilege.
587	S-mode CSRs (`satp`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`) are not transported. The
588	privilege level itself IS carried: an S/U-mode handoff also mirrors the
589	PMP configuration and requires an S/U-capable engine -- on an M-mode-only
590	engine the resume aborts with a clear pick-another-engine error. A
591	workload that traps, takes an interrupt, or switches privilege inside the
592	ROI is outside the contract. And because there is no hand-back leg,
593	nothing after the ROI executes.

597	## 7. Running on WSL2 and macOS
598	
599	**Linux** -- native, nothing to do.
600	
601	**Windows (WSL2)** -- works as Linux; two caveats:
602	
603	- Keep the repo and the mmap directories on the ext4 side (`~/...`), never
604	  under `/mnt/c` (drvfs is slow and shared mappings are not coherent there).
605	- `/dev/shm` is capped by the WSL VM memory. Raise `memory=` in
606	  `%UserProfile%\.wslconfig` if tier 1 is too small -- or let the tier list
607	  fall through to `~/.cache/andesim` automatically.
608	
609	`./andesim doctor` checks both (see its `mmap tiers:` section and WSL
610	warnings).
611	
612	**macOS** -- run-only. The engines are Linux binaries, so `./andesim`
613	transparently re-execs the run inside a prebuilt Linux runtime image in
614	the podman machine VM. One-time setup:
615	
616	```sh
617	brew install podman
618	podman machine init --memory 4096
619	podman machine start
620	podman pull <runtime image>      # or load a CI-built andesim-runtime:latest
621	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 256M my.elf
622	```
623	
624	Knobs: `ANDESIM_IMAGE` (image name, default `andesim-runtime:latest`),
625	`ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE` (container `/dev/shm`, default `3g`),
626	`ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE` (podman/docker). Your current directory is
627	bind-mounted at the same path, so relative ELF paths and output files
628	work. Apple Silicon runs the x86-64 image under emulation -- expect slower
629	wall-clock than a Linux host.

633	## 8. Troubleshooting
634	
635	| Symptom | Meaning / fix |
636	|---------|----------------|
637	| `multiple cycle-accurate engines; select one with --engine (have: ...)` | More than one engine is installed. Add `--engine <id>` from `list engines`. |
638	| `ELF is rv32 but engine '...' is rv64 -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF` | Width mismatch caught up front. Rebuild the ELF for the engine's width or pick the other engine. |
639	| `--trigger marker\|pc is required (the ROI delimiter; ...)` | Hybrid always needs the ROI delimiter: `--trigger marker` (markers in source) or `--trigger pc --pc-start S --pc-end E`. |
640	| The run never reaches the ROI / hangs until timeout | The start trigger never fired: the binary has no markers (marker mode), or `--pc-start` is never executed. Check with `--trigger pc` on a PC you know retires, or run `./build/hotloops` to find real hot PCs. |
641	| `symbol '<x>' not defined in <elf>` / `malformed address '<x>'` | `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` must be a defined symbol or a valid `0x` literal. |
642	| `--pc-start and --pc-end resolve to the same address ... (an empty ROI measures nothing)` | Pick two distinct boundaries; equal ones would measure nothing. |
643	| `--mem-size ...` rejected, or `raise --mem-size or shrink the image` | Hybrid caps at `2G` minus 4 KiB (use `2047M`), and the ELF's static image must fit below the reserved V-scratch page. |
644	| The mmap chose a disk directory (`[andesim] mmap ...` at `--log-level 1`), or `HSIM_MMAP_DIR` run fails | `/dev/shm` was too small for the request. Either accept the disk tier, free RAM, or pin a big non-tmpfs directory via `HSIM_MMAP_DIR`. |
645	| `warning: the program wrote CSRs engine ... does not implement: ...` | The figure may not represent this program on this engine (on silicon those writes would trap). Choose an engine implementing those CSRs, or drop the writes. |
646	| `multiple ... markers in ELF -- use --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...` (with `--kanata`) | Kanata needs a unique exit; switch to `--trigger pc` and name the exit with `--pc-end`. |
647	| `hybrid` rejects `-- <args>` | By design: hybrid owns both legs' command lines. Use the dedicated flags instead. |
648	| Missing artifact / engine not discovered | Run `./andesim doctor`; it names exactly what is missing and where it looked. Setup/build is covered in `README.md`. |
649	| A hybrid leg failed and you want to report or debug it | The run printed `[andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at <dir>` -- that directory holds the evidence and `manifest.txt` has each leg's exact command (newest 20 kept). Re-run with `--log-file run.log` (and `--log-level 1` for live engine logs) for the full picture. |
650	
651	---
652	
653	## 9. Deeper reading
654	
655	- `docs/hybrid_marker_quickstart.ipynb` -- runnable notebook version of
656	  the hybrid + marker flow, with captured real output (serve it with
657	  `scripts/notebook_server.sh`).

660	- `docs/hotloops.md` -- the hot-loop detector's full reference.
661	- `docs/engine_interface.md` -- how a new simulator joins andesim (for

# andesim User Guide

Audience: an engineer who wants to RUN programs on the Andes simulators
through `./andesim` and measure cycle counts. This guide covers every
user-facing option and feature.

It assumes andesim and its engines are already installed and built
(QEMU, the vsim engines, the plugin, the runtime, and the test ELFs are
prebuilt). If something is missing, run `./andesim doctor` and hand the
report to whoever owns your install; building is covered in `README.md`,
not here.

---

## 1. What andesim is

andesim runs one RISC-V ELF on one of three models:

| Model    | What runs                              | Speed          | You get                    |
|----------|----------------------------------------|----------------|-----------------------------|
| `fast`   | QEMU only (functional)                 | MHz-class      | program output, fast        |
| `cycle`  | one cycle-accurate engine, from reset  | kHz-class      | program output + total cycles |
| `hybrid` | QEMU fast-forwards, then the cycle engine measures one region you choose | fast until your region | program output + cycles of JUST your region |

`hybrid` is the headline feature: QEMU races through boot and setup, then
hands the complete architectural state and memory to the cycle-accurate
engine (vsim, built from the real RTL), which runs only your
region-of-interest (ROI). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta
across that window. You mark the window with a **trigger**: source-level
markers or a pair of PCs (section 5.3).

One run models ONE core. The cycle engine defines the hardware (ISA,
VLEN, caches); in hybrid mode the QEMU leg automatically inherits that
engine's ISA and VLEN so both legs execute the same architecture.

---

## 2. Check your installation

```sh
./andesim doctor          # read-only health report
./andesim list models     # the three models
./andesim list engines    # every engine you can pass to --engine
```

`doctor` checks artifacts, toolchain, runtime, engines, and the shared-memory
backing tiers, and prints WSL2 advice where relevant. A healthy install ends
with `Summary: N PASS, 0 FAIL`.

`list engines` shows what `--engine` accepts:

```
ENGINE                 TYPE  KIND            XLEN  VLEN  DLEN  ELEN
qemu64                 qemu  functional      64    -     -     -
qemu32                 qemu  functional      32    -     -     -
vsim:ax45mpv_premium   vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
vsim:ax46mpv_advanced  vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
```

`qemu64`/`qemu32` are the functional engines (`fast`); the `vsim:<cfg>`
entries are the cycle-accurate engines (`cycle`, and the measuring leg of
`hybrid`). `-` means the engine does not report that parameter.

Run `./andesim run -h` any time for the compact flag list; this guide is
the long version.

---

## 3. First runs

The install ships ready-made ELFs under `tests/fixtures/`; the examples
below use them. Replace with your own ELF once you have one (section 4).

### 3.1 fast -- functional, full speed

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
```

```
hello from vplat
```

Output is the program's own output, verbatim (QEMU passthrough). The exit
code of your program becomes the process exit code.

### 3.2 cycle -- one engine, from reset, total cycles

```sh
./andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
```

```
hello from vplat
[andesim] 4247 cycles
```

The engine's startup banner and verbose info log are filtered out so the
result stands alone; real warnings/errors still pass through, and the
program's exit code is propagated. The figure is the whole run from reset
-- boot, runtime init, everything.

### 3.3 hybrid -- fast-forward, then measure your region

`hybrid` needs a trigger that says where the measured window starts and
ends. The fixture below already contains ROI markers, so `--trigger
marker` works out of the box:

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
```

```
hello from QEMU1
[andesim] 54 cycles
```

Reading the output:

- `hello from QEMU1` is the program's own output from the fast leg.
- `[andesim] 54 cycles` is the answer: your ROI took 54 cycles on
  this engine. It is the vsim `mcycle` delta across the window (the same
  line shape `cycle` mode prints, but here it covers JUST your ROI).
- The run ends after the ROI. Code after your ROI never executes in a
  hybrid run -- hybrid is a measuring tool, not a way to finish the program.
- Want more detail? `--log-level 1` (section 5.10) adds the driver's
  chatter: the resolved engine/VLEN/trigger banner and the shared-memory
  line (`[andesim] mmap ...`, section 5.4).

The first hybrid run of a given (engine, ELF) pair is a few seconds slower:
andesim captures the engine's reset state once and caches it under
`~/.cache/andesim/` so later runs can skip restoring registers that still
hold reset values (typically ~4x faster on the vsim leg). The cache
refreshes itself when the engine or the ELF changes.

---

## 4. Prepare your own program

### 4.1 Compile once, run on every engine

Link against the andesim runtime and one ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
and across a `hybrid` handoff -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting:

```sh
riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \
  -B <andesim>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
```

- Use your Andes RISC-V GCC (the one `./andesim doctor` reports).
- `-B` points gcc at the runtime artifacts; use the absolute path when
  compiling outside the repo.
- `-specs=andesim.specs` swaps in the runtime's `crt0.o`, links
  `andesim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and pins the library order, so no
  semihosting library can leak into the link.
- Add `v` to `-march` (e.g. `rv64gcv`) for RVV code.

For rv32 targets use the rv32 compiler and the rv32 runtime flavor:

```sh
riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O2 \
  -B <andesim>/build/runtime/rv32 -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
```

Custom build system (no gcc driver)? Link the pieces directly:

```sh
... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andesim.ld \
  build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
  -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
```

What the runtime gives your program, on every engine:

| Channel          | Behavior                                                       |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| stdio (fd 0-2)   | `printf` etc. go to the simulator console (a modeled UART)     |
| exit code        | `exit(n)` (n < 256) terminates the simulation; `n` becomes the simulator process exit code |
| file io (fd > 2) | `open`/`read`/`write` pass through to host files, resolved against the engine's working directory |

A `printf` inside a measured ROI works -- but it adds the real UART cycles
to your figure. Keep measured kernels I/O-free when you want clean numbers.

### 4.2 Mark your region (ROI markers)

For `--trigger marker`, wrap the region you want to measure:

```c
#include <andesim/ROI.h>   /* shipped with the runtime; rides the -B flag */

andesim_ROI_begin();
my_kernel(a, b, c);
andesim_ROI_end();
```

The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (architectural NOPs), so a marker
binary also runs unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and on real silicon.
Ship one binary; measure when you want.

> **Measurement hygiene:** keep the kernel anchored inside the marker span
> -- read its inputs and write its outputs through memory inside the span,
> or wrap the kernel in a `__attribute__((noinline))` function called
> between the markers. The markers pin memory I/O but not register-only
> compute, so a kernel that carries live values in registers across the
> boundary may be hoisted or sunk out of the measured window by the
> compiler.

### 4.3 Cannot edit the binary? Use PC boundaries

`--trigger pc` needs no markers: you name the window with `--pc-start` and
`--pc-end`, each a symbol name or a `0x` address (section 5.3). To find
the hot region of an unknown binary first, run the bundled detector:

```sh
./build/hotloops --min-iters 10 my_kernel.elf
```

It runs the binary fast and reports the hottest loops (function, source
line, PC range) with a ready `measure:` line -- a `--pc-start`/`--pc-end`
pair you can paste straight into the hybrid command. See `docs/hotloops.md`
for the full flag reference.

---

## 5. The `run` options, one by one

Synopsis:

```
./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [options] <ELF> [-- <engine args>]
```

`run` is the default command -- you may omit it. `./andesim --mode fast
my.elf` and `./andesim my.elf --mode fast` both work; only the explicit
commands (`list`, `doctor`) are recognized by name.

### 5.1 `--mode fast|cycle|hybrid` (required)

Picks the model (section 1). Everything else keys off this choice.

### 5.2 `--engine <id>`

Picks the engine from `./andesim list engines`.

- `fast`: optional. The driver auto-selects `qemu64` or `qemu32` to match
  your ELF's width; an explicit `--engine qemu32|qemu64` overrides (with a
  warning if it disagrees with the ELF).
- `cycle` / `hybrid`: names the cycle-accurate engine. Optional only when
  exactly one is installed; with several you must choose:

  ```
  andesim run --mode cycle: model cycle: multiple cycle-accurate engines;
  select one with --engine (have: vsim:ax45mpv_premium, vsim:ax46mpv_advanced)
  ```

Width rules: `cycle`/`hybrid` reject an ELF whose width does not match the
engine, up front:

```
andesim run --mode cycle: ELF is rv32 but engine 'vsim:ax45mpv_premium' is rv64
  -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF
```

Hybrid additionally requires an rv64 engine (the fast leg is rv64; an rv32
engine cannot share architectural state with it and is rejected).

VLEN: each vsim engine has a fixed VLEN (see `list engines`); in hybrid
mode the QEMU leg inherits the engine's ISA and VLEN automatically, so
both legs execute identical architecture. Supported VLEN range in hybrid:
128 to 1024 bits. A standalone `fast` run defaults to the vector-capable
`andes-ax46mpv` (rv64) / `andes-a46mpv` (rv32) CPU model; to pin an exact
VLEN there, append a `-cpu` through the passthrough tail (the last `-cpu`
wins):

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax46mpv,vlen=256
```

### 5.3 `--trigger marker|pc` (+ `--pc-start`, `--pc-end`) -- hybrid only, required

The ROI delimiter for `--mode hybrid`.

**`--trigger marker`** (recommended when you can edit the source): the
window is the span strictly between `andesim_ROI_begin()` and
`andesim_ROI_end()` (section 4.2). The markers themselves are NOPs and
cost nothing.

**`--trigger pc`**: explicit boundaries, no source edits. Both flags are
required; each accepts a symbol name or a `0x` hex address:

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x1002cc my.elf
```

Semantics you should know:

- The instruction at `--pc-start` executes INSIDE the measured window (the
  fast leg stops just before it; the cycle engine resumes at it -- no
  instruction is lost across the handoff). `--pc-end` is where the window
  closes.
- Symbols are resolved from the ELF's own symbol table by the driver; no
  toolchain is needed at run time. A name that is not defined fails with
  `symbol '<x>' not defined in <elf>`; a bad literal fails with
  `malformed address '<x>'`.
- Both triggers are one-shot: the first hit of the start boundary opens the
  window, the first hit of the end boundary closes it. For a function called
  many times, the window is the FIRST call.
- Start and end must resolve to different addresses; an equal pair is an
  empty window and is rejected up front:
  `--pc-start and --pc-end resolve to the same address 0x... (an empty ROI measures nothing)`.

### 5.4 `--mem-size <spec>` -- guest memory

`SPEC` accepts `256M`, `1.5G`, `2G`, or raw bytes. Per-model meaning:

| Model    | Effect |
|----------|--------|
| `hybrid` | Your program RAM (default `128M`). Max `2G` minus 4 KiB: the driver reserves one page just above your RAM for the vector-register transport, so exactly `2G` is rejected (use `2047M`) and an ELF whose static image reaches into the reserved page is rejected with `raise --mem-size or shrink the image`. |
| `fast`   | Forwarded as a plain QEMU `-m`. No 2G cap; QEMU validates the size itself. |
| `cycle`  | Ignored (the engine always models its full DRAM window); the driver says so on stderr. |

Where the hybrid shared memory lives: andesim allocates a file both legs
map. It picks the first tier with enough free space (request + 256 MiB
headroom); run with `--log-level 1` to see which:

1. `/dev/shm` -- RAM-backed, fastest.
2. `~/.cache/andesim` -- disk-backed fallback (honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`).

```
[andesim] mmap 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))
```

Set `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/path` to pin one directory with NO fallback past it
(the run fails with a hint if it cannot hold the request). Do not pin a
tmpfs mount (`/tmp` on some distros) expecting a disk ceiling -- tmpfs is
still RAM.

### 5.5 `--print-memmap` -- which addresses may a hybrid workload touch?

Prints the guest memory map for exactly the run you are about to do (same
`--engine`/`--mem-size`; the ELF is optional and only adds a fit note),
then exits without running anything. Hybrid only.

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 128M
```

```
[andesim] hybrid memory map: engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium mem-size=128M
REGION           BASE         END          SIZE    TRANSPORT
DRAM             0x0          0x7ffffff    128M    shared mmap; content survives the handoff
V-scratch        0x8000000    0x8000fff    4K      reserved by the hybrid V transport; not program-usable
ILM              0x0          0xffff       64K     sidecar .ilm; DRAM overlay while milmb.IEN=1
DLM              0x200000     0x207fff     32K     sidecar .dlm; DRAM overlay while mdlmb.IEN=1
HVM              0x90000000   0x9003ffff   256K    sidecar .hvm
SimControl/HTIF  0xe0080000   0xe0080fff   4K      device; state does not cross the handoff
UART2            0xf0300000   0xf03fffff   1M      device (console); state does not cross the handoff
```

How to read it:

- END is the inclusive last byte.
- DRAM tracks `--mem-size`; the V-scratch page above it belongs to andesim.
- ILM/DLM/HVM rows appear only when the chosen engine has those memories
  and can transport their content; the addresses are the engine's own.
- Device state never crosses the handoff (each engine has its own UART and
  SimControl instance); only RAM content does.
- Anything NOT listed is unsupported in hybrid mode: it exists in one
  engine only, so touching it inside the ROI gives engine-specific behavior.

### 5.6 `--dry-run` -- preview without running

Valid in every mode: prints the exact engine command line(s), fully
resolved and shell-quoted, and runs nothing. `fast`/`cycle` print one
command; `hybrid` prints both legs. Use it to see precisely what a run
will execute, or to lift the command for your own scripting.

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --dry-run my.elf
# [andesim] dry-run: 2 command(s), not executed
# # command 1/2: fast-leg [qemu64]
# qemu-system-riscv64 ... -plugin .../libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=...
# # command 2/2: accurate-leg [vsim:ax45mpv_premium]
# sim_ax45mpv_premium my.elf --resume-from-qemu ... --handoff-out ...
```

### 5.7 `--verify` -- cross-check a hybrid run against a QEMU oracle

A hybrid run normally proves only that a cycle figure came out. `--verify`
(hybrid only, default off) re-runs the same ELF on pure QEMU up to the ROI
exit and compares the architectural state field by field against what the
cycle engine drained:

```
[andesim] 46 cycles
[state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match (counters and passthrough CSRs excluded)
[verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle
```

A mismatch lists each differing field and exits non-zero:

```
[state-diff] x10: ref=0x3d got=0x0
[state-diff] FAIL: 1 mismatch(es) (115 fields compared)
```

What is compared: the PC, all GPRs, FPRs (when FP state is live), the
vector registers and V CSRs (when V is live), the privilege level, and the
M-mode CSRs that round-trip through the handoff. Deliberately excluded:
`mcycle`/`minstret` (the engines count differently by design), `mip`
(hardware-driven pending bits), and a few CSRs whose reset values
legitimately differ between engines.

Two costs: one extra QEMU run of the whole program (cheap), and a full
register read-back over the Debug Module at the ROI exit (not cheap --
without `--verify` the exit drain reads only the two counters). Expect a
`--verify` run to take noticeably longer; the cycle figure itself is not
affected.

Related, printed on EVERY hybrid run (not just `--verify`): andesim tracks
which config CSRs your program actually wrote during the fast leg and
warns if any of them do not exist on the chosen cycle engine:

```
[andesim] warning: the program wrote CSRs engine vsim:<engine> does not
implement: <names> (on this engine's silicon these writes would trap; the
hybrid restore skipped them)
```

That means your program, on that engine's real silicon, would trap before
the ROI -- pick an engine that implements those CSRs, or drop the writes.
A clean run prints nothing.

### 5.8 `--kanata <file>` (+ `--objdump <file>`) -- pipeline trace of the ROI

Hybrid only (`--trigger marker|pc`). Writes a Kanata-format pipeline trace
covering exactly the measured window -- engine boot and handoff overhead
are filtered out. Open the file in
[Konata](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata) to see the pipeline.

```sh
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
  --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata
```

Add `--objdump <file>` (a text dump you generated once with
`riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d my.elf > my.S`) and the trace embeds the
disassembly next to each PC. `--objdump` requires `--kanata`.

Marker-mode constraint: the ELF must contain exactly one exit marker. With
more than one, the run errors out and tells you to use `--trigger pc` with
an explicit `--pc-end` instead.

### 5.9 `--gdb` (+ `--gdb-port <port>`) -- attach a debugger

Pauses the simulation at startup so a debugger can attach. Not available
in hybrid mode.

**fast** -- opens QEMU's GDB stub (default port 1234) and waits:

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast --gdb my.elf
# other terminal:
gdb-multiarch -ex 'target remote :1234' my.elf
```

**cycle** -- resets and HALTS the hart, opens the engine's JTAG bitbang
port (default 9104) in the background, then execs `$ICEMAN` -- your JTAG
debug server -- in the foreground. Point GDB at the server's own gdb port
(from your server config), not at 9104:

```sh
export ICEMAN=/path/to/jtag-debug-server
./andesim run --mode cycle --gdb --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium my.elf
```

`$ICEMAN` must speak the OpenOCD `remote_bitbang` protocol. A modern
**OpenOCD (0.12+)** works: a one-line wrapper can `exec openocd -f <cfg>`
where `<cfg>` sets `adapter driver remote_bitbang`, `remote_bitbang port
9104`, a generic `riscv` target, and a `gdb_port`. Note: the OpenOCD 0.10
bundled with Andes ICEman has a `remote_bitbang` bug against this DTM --
use a current OpenOCD.

`--gdb-port` overrides the port (fast: the QEMU stub port; cycle: the
JTAG bitbang port).

### 5.10 `--log-level <0-6>` (+ `--log-file`) -- how much andesim says

The same scale as the vsim engines' own `--log-level`, so you learn one
scheme: `0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off`.
Default is `2` (info): you see your program's output, the answer line
(`[andesim] N cycles`), and any warnings or errors -- nothing else.

`--log-level 1` (debug) adds the driver's chatter: the hybrid banner
(engine/VLEN/trigger), the decision lines (which engine and why; what
your `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` resolved to), the shared-mmap line (section
5.4), the window detail (`[andesim] window: trigger=... vsim mcycle=...
qemu mcycle=...`), and the closing PASS line. The level also rides into
both hybrid legs: the vsim engine gets the same `--log-level`, the QEMU
handoff plugin gets `log_level=`, and their stderr streams live to your
terminal (at info and above it is silenced), so one flag tunes the whole
pipeline.

`--log-level 0` (trace) additionally prints, just before each engine
spawns, its fully resolved command line -- the hybrid legs (`[andesim]
exec fast-leg [qemu64]: ...`) and the standalone fast/cycle runs
(`[andesim] exec standalone [qemu64]: ...`) alike. It is the same text
`--dry-run` shows, copy-pasteable to re-run one engine by hand, and it
is emitted BEFORE the spawn, so even a hung run leaves the command in
the log.

`--log-file <file>` appends EVERY level's messages -- timestamped and
level-tagged, regardless of the console `--log-level` -- to `<file>`.
Run once with `--log-file`, attach the file to a bug report, and nothing
needs re-running. Your program's own output is never filtered at any
level.

Related (always on, any level): when a hybrid leg fails, andesim keeps
the run's evidence -- the drained state files, LM sidecars, the staged
QEMU config, a copy of your ELF, and a `manifest.txt` with the error and
every leg's exact command -- under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` (newest 20
kept) and prints where:

```
[andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at /home/u/.cache/andesim/repro/20260711T081500Z-my_prog (see manifest.txt)
```

### 5.11 `-- <args...>` -- engine passthrough

Everything after a bare `--` is forwarded verbatim to the engine.
`fast`/`cycle` only: those modes run one engine process, so there is an
unambiguous target (see the VLEN example in 5.2). `hybrid` builds both
legs' command lines itself and REJECTS `--` args rather than guessing
which leg you meant -- use the dedicated flags (`--kanata`, `--objdump`,
`--mem-size`, ...) instead.

---

## 6. What a hybrid run does for you automatically

You normally do not need this section to use andesim -- it explains the
behaviors you will observe.

**Two legs, one state.** The fast leg (QEMU) runs to your ROI start, then
drains the complete architectural state -- GPRs, FPRs, vector registers,
CSRs (including the Andes-specific blocks), privilege level -- into a
state file. Program RAM is shared by construction (both legs map the same
file), so memory needs no copy. The cycle engine restores the state
through its Debug Module, runs your ROI, and drains the counters at the
exit trigger. The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta.

**Config that matters for timing rides along.** Cache-enable state (L1
`mcache_ctl`, and the L2 controller's config window on engines that have
an L2) is restored before the ROI, so a program that enabled caches during
boot measures WITH caches on -- not at the engine's reset default.

**Only what your program wrote is restored.** andesim records which config
CSRs the program actually wrote during the fast leg and restores only
those; an untouched CSR keeps the engine's own reset value, exactly like
that engine's real silicon. If the program wrote a CSR the engine does not
implement, you get the warning shown in section 5.7.

**Local memories travel too.** On engines with ILM/DLM (tightly-coupled
memories) or HVM (high-bandwidth vector memory), their content is drained
from the fast leg and loaded into the cycle engine before resume, so a
program that stages code or data there before the ROI resumes with it in
place. (A program using ILM/DLM must enable them itself via
`milmb`/`mdlmb`, as real TCM firmware does; that write is restored
automatically.) `--print-memmap` shows whether your engine has these
regions.

**First-run baseline capture.** Restoring a register over the Debug Module
costs hundreds of simulated cycles, and most state still holds reset
values. The first hybrid run of a given (engine build, ELF) pair captures
the engine's reset state once and caches it under `~/.cache/andesim/`
(honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`); later runs skip the no-op restores, typically
cutting the vsim leg ~4x. The cache invalidates itself when the engine or
ELF changes; delete the directory to force a fresh capture. This never
changes results -- a restore is skipped only when the value is already
there.

**The ROI envelope (limits).** The measured window is assumed bare-metal,
single-hart, trap-free, interrupt-free, paging-off, and single-privilege.
S-mode CSRs (`satp`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`) are not transported. The
privilege level itself IS carried: an S/U-mode handoff also mirrors the
PMP configuration and requires an S/U-capable engine -- on an M-mode-only
engine the resume aborts with a clear pick-another-engine error. A
workload that traps, takes an interrupt, or switches privilege inside the
ROI is outside the contract. And because there is no hand-back leg,
nothing after the ROI executes.

---

## 7. Running on WSL2 and macOS

**Linux** -- native, nothing to do.

**Windows (WSL2)** -- works as Linux; two caveats:

- Keep the repo and the mmap directories on the ext4 side (`~/...`), never
  under `/mnt/c` (drvfs is slow and shared mappings are not coherent there).
- `/dev/shm` is capped by the WSL VM memory. Raise `memory=` in
  `%UserProfile%\.wslconfig` if tier 1 is too small -- or let the tier list
  fall through to `~/.cache/andesim` automatically.

`./andesim doctor` checks both (see its `mmap tiers:` section and WSL
warnings).

**macOS** -- run-only. The engines are Linux binaries, so `./andesim`
transparently re-execs the run inside a prebuilt Linux runtime image in
the podman machine VM. One-time setup:

```sh
brew install podman
podman machine init --memory 4096
podman machine start
podman pull <runtime image>      # or load a CI-built andesim-runtime:latest
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 256M my.elf
```

Knobs: `ANDESIM_IMAGE` (image name, default `andesim-runtime:latest`),
`ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE` (container `/dev/shm`, default `3g`),
`ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE` (podman/docker). Your current directory is
bind-mounted at the same path, so relative ELF paths and output files
work. Apple Silicon runs the x86-64 image under emulation -- expect slower
wall-clock than a Linux host.

---

## 8. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Meaning / fix |
|---------|----------------|
| `multiple cycle-accurate engines; select one with --engine (have: ...)` | More than one engine is installed. Add `--engine <id>` from `list engines`. |
| `ELF is rv32 but engine '...' is rv64 -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF` | Width mismatch caught up front. Rebuild the ELF for the engine's width or pick the other engine. |
| `--trigger marker\|pc is required (the ROI delimiter; ...)` | Hybrid always needs the ROI delimiter: `--trigger marker` (markers in source) or `--trigger pc --pc-start S --pc-end E`. |
| The run never reaches the ROI / hangs until timeout | The start trigger never fired: the binary has no markers (marker mode), or `--pc-start` is never executed. Check with `--trigger pc` on a PC you know retires, or run `./build/hotloops` to find real hot PCs. |
| `symbol '<x>' not defined in <elf>` / `malformed address '<x>'` | `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` must be a defined symbol or a valid `0x` literal. |
| `--pc-start and --pc-end resolve to the same address ... (an empty ROI measures nothing)` | Pick two distinct boundaries; equal ones would measure nothing. |
| `--mem-size ...` rejected, or `raise --mem-size or shrink the image` | Hybrid caps at `2G` minus 4 KiB (use `2047M`), and the ELF's static image must fit below the reserved V-scratch page. |
| The mmap chose a disk directory (`[andesim] mmap ...` at `--log-level 1`), or `HSIM_MMAP_DIR` run fails | `/dev/shm` was too small for the request. Either accept the disk tier, free RAM, or pin a big non-tmpfs directory via `HSIM_MMAP_DIR`. |
| `warning: the program wrote CSRs engine ... does not implement: ...` | The figure may not represent this program on this engine (on silicon those writes would trap). Choose an engine implementing those CSRs, or drop the writes. |
| `multiple ... markers in ELF -- use --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...` (with `--kanata`) | Kanata needs a unique exit; switch to `--trigger pc` and name the exit with `--pc-end`. |
| `hybrid` rejects `-- <args>` | By design: hybrid owns both legs' command lines. Use the dedicated flags instead. |
| Missing artifact / engine not discovered | Run `./andesim doctor`; it names exactly what is missing and where it looked. Setup/build is covered in `README.md`. |
| A hybrid leg failed and you want to report or debug it | The run printed `[andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at <dir>` -- that directory holds the evidence and `manifest.txt` has each leg's exact command (newest 20 kept). Re-run with `--log-file run.log` (and `--log-level 1` for live engine logs) for the full picture. |

---

## 9. Deeper reading

- `docs/hybrid_marker_quickstart.ipynb` -- runnable notebook version of
  the hybrid + marker flow, with captured real output (serve it with
  `scripts/notebook_server.sh`).
- `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md` -- one guided exercise per trigger
  mode, with drill-down on the underlying commands.
- `docs/hotloops.md` -- the hot-loop detector's full reference.
- `docs/engine_interface.md` -- how a new simulator joins andesim (for
  engine vendors/integrators, not needed to run workloads).
- `README.md` -- what the workspace contains and how it is built.
